title: Feminism, or the Death of Love: Masculinity & Femininity's Great ...
summary: Part two of his Nietzsche-based series on women: he argues that pushing women into the workforce (industrial revolution, world wars, backed by financial interests) blurred the masculine/feminine roles and killed romance, producing 'heterofatalism'. He frames men as tools and women as art, says love starts as conditional lust before maturing, and calls on men to take responsibility for restoring relationships.
claims: The series aims to restore men's respect and healthy adoration for women rather than bash them; you cannot cherish what you do not respect
Historically women used their seductive power sparingly and pretended not to have it; mystery was essential to feminine power
Cam girls and streamers monetize seduction while men get nothing in return; this imbalance creates heterofatalism, where men and women want each other but cannot connect
Feminism did not appear out of nowhere: women were persuaded that feminine power was worth less than masculine power and traded theirs away
Drawing on Nietzsche, women were the aristocratic gender who got men to do the work, while men are the laborious plebeian gender
Women entering the workforce was pushed by banks and political powers seeking double the accounts and taxes, in two phases: industrial revolution and the world wars
The feminization of the workforce produced modern work-resistant culture; the psychological notion of stress is in his view a female concept
Symbolically men are tools (a hammer) and women are art (a painting); a woman's beauty remains her top attraction trait, a man's function and character his
Many men misunderstand female sexual selection by putting all their stock in looks, projecting their own criteria onto women
Society is built around protecting women and men are expendable; the pyramid of preciousness runs pregnant women, children, elderly, women, then men at the bottom
Feminism speaks of women's rights but never of duties, though rights always come with responsibilities
Love must exist beyond good and evil; a materialistic, scientific calculation of relationships concludes they are not worth it
Content that dissects exactly what women like deromanticizes them; let women keep part of their mystery
Peacock theory: the pursuing sex develops attributes based on what it believes the other sex likes; traits that make a man masculine to men also attract women
Japan's herbivore men show what happens when males stop pursuing: they take no risks and stay single
The alpha male crisis comes from men copying the visible traits of attractive men when what actually attracts is their function
Love starts conditional, as biological lust; when novelty fades, mature love can replace it, but without initial attraction love can never begin
It is the balancing act, not balance itself, that makes love; giving the other too much too freely spoils the relationship
Most of what men do, such as lifting or chasing a better job or car, ultimately serves to raise their value with women
Porn and cam girls make young men lustful creatures and sever the roots of love; sensuality forces love to grow too fast with weak roots
Sex should be the result of a blossoming love, not the fertilizer; relationships that start with first-date sex last about two weeks
Capitalism turned women's bodies into money-making machines; during COVID many women turned to OnlyFans
Feminism is a tantrum that started when men stopped providing resistance; since the maiden is blindfolded and the knight is not, fixing it is men's responsibility
Today's economy makes a single-income household nearly impossible, closing the trap even for women who would prefer not to work
The line 'a woman needs a man like a fish needs a bicycle' haunted him for ten years; he reads it as coming from a disappointed woman
Porn and social media now satisfy biological urges, yet people are miserable, proving love is more than meeting conditions
He recorded the second half the next day in 105F heat amid forest fires, with 110F in his garage
